newsitem.title: USA: Chemicals tanker runs aground off Florida.
newsitem.headline: Chemicals tanker runs aground off Florida.

text.p: A German-flagged tanker loaded with potentially explosive chemicals has run aground about three miles (5 km) south of Cape Florida, the U.S. Coast Guard said on Thursday.

A barge was alongside the Igloo Moon trying to unload some of the three million gallons (11 million litres) of liquid butadiene cargo in order to refloat the vessel, Coast Guard Petty Officer Veronica Colbath told Reuters.
"They still don't know how or why it ran aground," she said.
The Igloo Moon was travelling from the Middle East to Houston when it became trapped on Wednesday in about 25 feet (7.6 metres) of water off Key Biscayne near Miami.
The Coast Guard has set up a one-mile (1.6 km) safety zone while the barge attempts the unloading operation.
"It's going to be an all-day thing. They have to deal with the weather, which could change, and they can't take on too much or they'll be in the same predicament," Colbath said.
The gas, which is used to make rubber, was potentially explosive but was at present stable, she said.
The 464-foot (141 metre) vessel is owned by a company named Martin.
